Hi Sarah — thanks for sending the sample. Quick responses inline and an attached high-level plan (ACME_embed_backfill_plan_v1.pdf):

- Backfill timing: rough estimate for continuous backfill with dedicated capacity (8 x A100 equivalent) is ~18-22 hours for 50M small docs (avg 400 tokens). If you need a conservative plan w/ burst windows off, we can provide a phased timeline (wave 1: priority corpora — 0–10M; wave 2: remaining).

- Vector DB recommendation: because of audit/logging requirements we recommend managed + VPC peering to your cloud account (Redwood Dedicated + customer-managed logging) OR self-hosted Milvus with our audit-forwarding integration. Tradeoffs attached in the plan: managed = lower ops and consistent backups; self-hosted = more control for retention windows and HSM/KMS integration.

- Rerank evals: included a suggested acceptance checklist in the attached doc and a short MD with sample prompts. We'll also include an initial smoke-test eval set (100 queries + human label pass).

Proposed pre-read: ACME_embed_backfill_plan_v1.pdf, rerank-eval-criteria.md. Can we lock a 45-min sync Monday 11:00am PDT?

Thanks — cc'ing Marissa to confirm DB tradeoffs and Mina for QA/eval scope.

Best,
Monica Patel

Sarah — a couple of technical clarifications from our infra perspective:

- Document size distribution matters a lot. If 75% of your docs are small (<= 512 tokens) our estimates skew lower; if you have many long clinical notes (2k+ tokens) embedding compute and chunking will increase overall time. The sample looked mixed — please confirm percentile sizes.

- Vector DB options:
  * Managed (our Dedicated-backed store): we handle replication, snapshotting, and provide token-level cost breakdowns. Good for faster time-to-prod and SLA-backed availability.
  * Self-hosted (Milvus/Weaviate): gives you direct control over maintenance windows and network isolation. We'll provide ops playbooks for indexing and incremental rehydration.

- Backfill approach: recommend incremental seed->validate->promote waves (5–10M per wave) with automatic KV-cache priming for hot queries. This reduces regression risk during cutover.

I'll bring a short tech-decision matrix to the call to capture your preference.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick answers from infra:

- Payload characteristics: 50M total, 60% < 1KB, 30% 1–5KB, 10% >5KB (clinical transcripts). We can provide a histogram dump if needed (attached sample payloads.csv is a 1k sample).

- Compliance: we require HSM-backed KMS for key material and full audit logs (S3 access logs + DB query audit). We prefer self-hosted unless Redwood can guarantee those controls in Dedicated.

- Rerank acceptance: our PM wants: precision@5 delta <= 2% vs current baseline, median latency (query + rerank) < 280ms P50, and no critical regressions on top-10 retrieval for 100 core queries. Please confirm whether the smoke-test you mentioned will cover these metrics.

Tom Wallace
